subject: Archaeology
title: LiDAR Reveals a Maya Megacity
description: A 60-second lesson on LiDAR Reveals a Maya Megacity.

hook.text: In 2018, lasers fired from airplanes over Guatemala's jungle revealed something no one expected.

buildup.text: LiDAR stripped away the tree canopy digitally, exposing 60,000 hidden structures beneath the forest.

discovery.text: Roads, fortresses, farms, and pyramids appeared — a Maya civilization far larger than anyone had estimated.

twist.text: The data showed the Maya lowlands held up to 11 million people, not the 1–2 million previously believed.

climax.text: One scan in weeks accomplished what would have taken a century of jungle trekking on foot.

punchline.text: Lasers from the sky rewrote what we knew about an entire civilization.

quiz.question: What did the 2018 LiDAR survey of Guatemala's jungle reveal?
options: A single massive pyramid larger than any previously known
60,000 hidden structures showing the Maya civilization was far larger than estimated
Evidence of a previously unknown civilization predating the Maya

details.summary: In 2018, LiDAR surveys over the Guatemalan jungle revealed an interconnected Maya civilization of over 60,000 structures — causeways, fortifications, farms, and cities — hidden beneath the forest canopy. The discovery tripled estimates of the Maya population in the Classic period.
details.whyItMatters: LiDAR proved that the Maya civilization was vastly larger and more interconnected than ground-based archaeology had ever suggested. It transformed our understanding of one of the Americas' greatest civilizations virtually overnight.
takeaways: LiDAR revealed over 60,000 hidden Maya structures in Guatemala
It tripled population estimates for the Maya Classic period
The technology sees through dense jungle canopy to the ground

faq.question: How does LiDAR see through jungle canopy?
faq.answer: LiDAR fires millions of laser pulses from aircraft. Some pulses penetrate gaps in vegetation and reflect off the ground surface. Software strips away vegetation returns to reveal bare-earth terrain models showing roads, buildings, reservoirs, and field systems invisible from the ground.

faq.question: What did the LiDAR survey reveal about Maya civilization?
faq.answer: It showed cities connected by wide raised causeways, massive irrigation systems, defensive walls, and intensive agriculture covering areas previously thought to be empty jungle. The Maya lowlands supported millions of people in a sophisticated, interconnected urban landscape.
